population.definition: 2017 census count (census night 11 May 2017) for Mbabane as listed in a table of cities and urban centres compiled from Central Statistical Office results; the page does not define city vs urban-area boundary. Not the national statistics office page itself. Municipal estimates of 80,000-95,000 (no year) are mentioned by the government page but are not census.

source.title: Eswatini: cities and urban centers (census table)
source.publisher: citypopulation.de (credits Central Statistical Office Swaziland)
source.quote: Central Statistical Office Swaziland

facts.claim: Mbabane was conferred city status in 1992, which created the Mbabane City Council.

source.title: MBABANE: FROM TOWN TO CAPITAL CITY
source.publisher: Government of Eswatini, Ruby Jubilee site (40years.gov.sz)
source.quote: City status in 1992 marked a defining milestone in Mbabane's modern growth story.

facts.claim: When King Mswati III took the throne in 1986, Mbabane was still largely an administrative town; population grew from about 38,290 (1986) to 60,691 (2017).

source.title: MBABANE: FROM TOWN TO CAPITAL CITY
source.publisher: Government of Eswatini, Ruby Jubilee site (40years.gov.sz)
source.quote: Population grew from about 38,290 in 1986 to over 60,691 in 2017.

facts.claim: Mbabane's history is traced to Chief Mbabane Kunene, who settled the area in the 1750s (the likely origin of the name; the tourism page does not explicitly say the town was named for him).

source.title: Mbabane | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website (Eswatini Tourism Authority logo)
source.quote: Mbabane's history dates back to the 1750s, when Chief Mbabane Kunene settled in the area.

facts.claim: The British moved the administrative capital of Swaziland from Manzini to Mbabane after the Boer War damaged Manzini.

source.title: Mbabane, Eswatini
source.publisher: EBSCO Research Starters
source.author: Lynn-nore Chittom
source.quote: the British leaders moved the administrative capital of Swaziland from the city of Manzini to Mbabane

facts.claim: The Manzini municipal council records that after the Anglo-Boer war ended in May 1902, British settlers preferred the highveld for the administrative capital.

source.title: History of Manzini
source.publisher: Municipal Council of Manzini
source.quote: the new British settlers preferred the highveld as the new administrative capital

places.name: Sibebe Rock
places.what: A huge granite dome just north of Mbabane, a popular hiking destination. The tourism board calls it one of southern Africa's most impressive geological features.

source.title: Sibebe Rock | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: just north of Mbabane

source.title: Sibebe Rock | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: rises to 1,488m

facts.label: Geology

source.title: Sibebe Rock | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website

places.name: Mantenga Nature Reserve and Cultural Village
places.what: A reserve in the Ezulwini Valley centred on Mantenga Falls. It includes a replica traditional Swazi village.

source.title: Mantenga Reserve, Village & Falls | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: Swaziland's largest waterfall by volume.

source.title: Mantenga Reserve, Village & Falls | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: replica mid-19th Century Swazi village, constructed using authentic materials and techniques.

source.title: Ezulwini Valley | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: Unspoilt woodlands with a traditional cultural village experience.

places.name: Swazi Candles Centre (Malkerns Valley)
places.what: A craft complex in the Malkerns Valley where artisans make candles, woodcarvings, beadwork and textiles. It also holds shops, a bookshop and the Yebo! Art Gallery.

source.title: Swazi Candles Centre | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: more like stepping into a colourful community than a typical craft market.

source.title: Swazi Candles Centre | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: hand-poured candles in unique shapes and colours make perfect keepsakes.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: claimed largest candle collection in Africa

source.title: Shopping | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: debatably the largest collection of candles you will find in Africa!

places.name: Eswatini National Museum (Lobamba)
places.what: The national museum, in siSwati Umsamo Wesive, stands in Lobamba, the royal and legislative capital near Mbabane. It is also headquarters of the Eswatini National Trust Commission.

source.title: Lobamba | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: known in siSwati as Umsamo Wesive was built in 1972

facts.label: Institution

source.title: Lobamba | The Kingdom of Eswatini (Swaziland)
source.publisher: The Kingdom of Eswatini tourism website
source.quote: It serves as the HQ of the Eswatini National Trust Commission (ENTC)

notNotFound: Mbabane Swazi Market: no readable source describing it beyond a one-line tourism-board mention of traditional markets (place omitted)
Indingilizi Gallery: only one Mail & Guardian line read (Nellie Bowles, 2011-11-11); too thin for a place entry
Name origin: only the tourism board's chief Mbabane Kunene 1750s line; no source explicitly states the town is named after him
Founding date: 1887 Mickey Wells claim seen only on aggregator/Wikipedia-derived pages, not used
Capital date conflict: 1902 (EBSCO, Manzini council context) vs 1903 (tourism board)
Population from national statistics office or UN directly: not found; value is from citypopulation.de crediting CSO, and matches 40years.gov.sz
Population definition: not stated by any readable source
Myth corrected by a source: none found
Sibebe Rock size: tourism page also says 16,500 ha, which looks inconsistent with a single dome and was not used
Commons photo for Swazi Candles is captioned Matsapha; location label may be inexact. No Commons file found for Mbabane market beyond a 1979 'Portable market hut' photo, or for the National Museum
